headline: New rabies vaccine shows promise in African trial
meta_description: A single-dose rabies vaccine proved safe and effective in Tanzanian adults and children, with antibody protection lasting a full year.
summary_short: A new single-dose rabies vaccine demonstrated safety and strong immune response in Tanzanian participants, with protection sustained after one year.
body:
A single-dose adenovirus-vectored rabies vaccine called ChAdOx2 RabG has shown encouraging results in trials with Tanzanian adults and children. The vaccine was safe and generated strong antibody responses in all participants tested.

What makes this development significant is the durability of protection. After one year, antibody levels in participants remained above protective thresholds—suggesting the vaccine could offer lasting defense against a disease that kills tens of thousands annually in Africa. For communities where rabies exposure is a real risk and access to traditional post-exposure prophylaxis is limited, a single-dose option represents a meaningful advance.

The successful trial in Tanzania demonstrates that this approach works across different age groups and populations, bringing hope for a simpler, more accessible rabies prevention tool.

Antibody protection sustained above threshold at one year
Safe profile with strong immune response
